title: Script screenshots
subject: Computing
unit: Spring 1: Variables in games and e-bullying
source: Seeded from computing/y6 lesson 6 (Script screenshots (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 6: Changing a variable when a sprite is clicked. To understand how an event changes the value of a variable

questions.q: Add 'when this sprite clicked, change score by 1' to the Apple.
questions.a: The score goes up by 1 per click.
questions.model: Teacher drags the hat block, snaps 'change score by 1', clicks the apple three times and reads the monitor.

questions.q: Add 'go to random position' after the change. What does it do?
questions.a: The apple jumps to a new place after each click.

questions.q: Why do we put 'set score to 0' under the green flag?
questions.a: So each new game starts from 0.

questions.q: Core: Make a 'click the apple' game: score up by 1 per click, apple jumps, score reset on the flag.
questions.a: Two scripts on the Apple: flag (set 0) and click (change by 1, random position).
questions.model: Teacher shows the flag script first.

questions.q: Extend: Add a Bowl sprite that takes away a point when clicked by mistake.
questions.a: Bowl: when this sprite clicked, change score by -1.

questions.q: Stretch: Make the apple say 'Well done!' when score reaches 10.
questions.a: if score = 10 then say 'Well done!' (inside the click script).

questions.q: Which block is an event? A) change score by 1 B) when this sprite clicked C) go to random position
Why must a game reset its score at the start?
questions.a: A variable keeps its last value, so without a reset it carries on from the last game.
